52.45084,1.55756: Dorothy Hodgkin 1910-1994 biochemist and Nobel Laureate who determined the structure of penicillin and vitamin B12 studied at this school 1921-1928
52.45507,1.55886: St. Mary's House (Grade II) From 1720, the Leper Hospital of St. Mary Magdalene stood on this site. Charles II gave the land to the Town. From 1846 - 1906, the building housed the Fauconberge Grammar School of Beccles.
52.45585,1.55999: Leman House (Grade I) An outstanding C16th building, remodelled in the Jacobean style. In 1631, it was endowed as a school by Sir John Leman, whose coat of arms adorns the North Gable.
52.4559,1.56425: Lloyd's Bank (Grade II) A Theatre was built here in 1819 by the actor, David Fisher. In 1845, it became the Corn Exchange and is now part of the present Bank. In the C16th, the Town Crane stood near this site.
52.45635,1.56076: The Old Rectory (Grade II) A fine Georgian house, built in 1789, reputedly for Philip Dykes, gent. From 1830, the residence of Mrs Elizabeth Stone. It was the Parish Rectory from 1879 until 1982.
52.4574,1.56222: Barclay's Bank The White Horse Inn stood here before 1760. It then became shop premises until replaced by the first purpose-built bank in the Town
52.45759,1.56319: The King's Head Hotel The earliest recorded reference to this Wetherspoon free house is a lease granted to George Cocke dated 1668. This Grade II listed building is described as "17th and 18th centuries, with alterations". The 18th century, Georgian style parts flank the earlier section of the building. The King's Head was a coaching inn, and until fairly recently, the main entrance facing New Market was an open archway, leading to a cobbled yard with galleries at the back and stables to the rear. These premises were refurbished and reopened by J.D. Whetherspoon in February 2013.
52.45761,1.56319: Principal Coaching Inn of Beccles in the eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries
52.4578,1.56201: Town Hall (Grade II) Built in 1765, in Gothic Revival style on the site of the old Market Cross, originally with an octagonal turret over the doorway Formerly the Shire Hall and Courthouse, it is now the Town Hall
52.4578,1.56419: Quaker Cottage (Grade II) This cottage, built in 1715, was given to the Quakers in 1759 by Philip Sewell, a local wool trader. The Friends Meeting House was built at the rear in 1744.
52.45801,1.56253: This plaque commemorates a life's work for mankind by Dr Dorothy Hodgkin OM FRS 1910-1994 Nobel Prize Winner 1964 Freeman of Beccles 1965 A former pupil of Sir John Leman Grammar School
52.45805,1.56421: The Public Hall Designed by Thomas Fulcher in 1785 as an assembly room and used for Balls, Corporation Feasts and as a Theatre. Restored in 1903, it is now the Town's Public Hall.
52.45808,1.56244: The White Swan (Grade II) There has been a tavern here since 1538. Owned by the Benay family (tanners) from 1673 for more than 100 years. Subsequently owned by Seth Land, Blacksmith, who also built Tower House opposite.
52.45812,1.56257: Issued to celebrate nine hundred years of Norman heritage This community is recorded in the Domesday Book 1086 Domesday 1086 - 1986
52.459,1.56303: Vicomte Francois Chateaubriand (1768-1848) The French writer, diplomat and Foreign Minister, lived here from 1793-1795. During this time, he taught in a local school
52.45944,1.5625: Site of the medieval chapel of St Peter
52.45947,1.56263: St. Peter's House (Grade I) Built on the site of a medieval church (sold in the reign of Henry VIII) The brick facade dates from the 1730s The magnificent Gothic Revival rooms at the rear were added 30 years later.
52.46048,1.56313: Adrian Bell The Suffolk writer, Adrian Bell, lived here from 1954 to 1964 In the C18th, many leather workers lived beside the river and this was the home of a glove and breeches maker
52.46098,1.56359: Co-operative Society Shop The town's first "Co-op" opened here in 1879. By 1899, growth in the business necessitated a move to a larger premises The new shop buildings in Smallgate were designed by Beccles architect, Arthur Pells
52.46213,1.56375: Oswald House (Grade II) Late C17th house with Flemish gables. Built by Joseph Harbor (tanner) In the mid C19th, it was the home of Robert Oswald (auctioneer), F.M. Sir Claud Auchinlech lived here 1960-1967
52.46225,1.56666: This pound was for confining all lost stray animals, particularly the horse. An impounded horse was very valuable being the solve means of transport, which demanded a substantial release fee to be paid to the Town Council. For many centuries this has been the site of the Pound and it was rescued in 1982 by the Town Council, Beccles Society and Voluntary subscriptions.
52.46227,1.56373: Montagu House (Grade II) Early C18th house with a fine Georgian facade. Home of the Montagu family, whose coat of arms is above the door. Captain Edward Montagu R.N., who served with valour in the Napoleonic Wars, lived here.
52.46457,1.74302: Benjamin Britten 1913-1976 composer and Freeman of the Borough of Lowestoft was born here on 22 November 1913 and grew up in this house
52.47427,1.75033: Lowestoft Railway Station Britain's most easterly railway station. The Reedham to Lowestoft line was commissioned by Sir Morton Peto and opened on 3rd May 1947. The present station was built in 1855 by Lucas Bros.
